summary:
I reviewed the whole slice (afd021d..e2431bc), not only attempt 3. The product code in src matches the design. It has eight departures, all declared in build attempt 2: the NotScanned flag instead of a new EntryKind, the pop-time check, the outside-defect Precautions switch (on by default, with the notice on screen), report fields as counts, and the others.

ContainerLayerStore.Resolve handles every spelling I traced: string step first, then the final path by handle, rebased into the root's spelling.
- The walk compares popped paths for equality without GetFullPath, so 'Layers.' and 'Layers ' stay safe.
- The DirectoryReader.Read backstop is the only open path, and the fitness rule enforces that.
- On Refuse nothing is listed. In the App, NotScanned rows never reach Unreadable and never get 'Show in Explorer'.

What I ran:
- Full suite: 549 passed, 3 failed. The 3 are the LastAccess/HeldOpenTree back-dating tests that failed before this slice.
- Acceptance repro: 1 passed, exit 0.
- Fitness: all 77 rules hold.

Every material row of the case matrix is fed by its test. I read each one; details are in `cases`.

One major defect is in the person-run judge, tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 -Report. It decides DONE (c), and it reads OUTCOME A / VERDICT PASS in two cases I built in hand-made run logs:
- a full exe run that crashed (exit 70, no report);
- a session with no exe runs at all.
It also never counts an exe arm's guard stop as over T, only L's. So the 'never PASS on missing data' promised by m7 (O-027) and N2 (O-043) does not hold for the exe runs.

Attempt 3 changed no src, but that was the 20-entry cap on the cases list, not a loop. Residue: my scratch folder %TEMP%\cr-sl095-f3crash (two jsonl files) could not be deleted (Access denied).

Second round: Second round found three new defects. All are in the person-run measurement harness, tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1. The product code in src held up under adversarial reading, and I found nothing new there:
- Resolve's string and handle steps, IsAtOrUnder's separator boundary, the backstop's -1 code and the App's NotScannedRow path all behave.
- The hook's folder-count and size-count parsers handle en-IN lakh grouping ("9,20,052").
- ScanArm's list-file halves are written and read consistently.

I ran -Report, robocopy and fltmc on hand-built inputs in %TEMP%.

1. **(major)** -Protocol takes I0 right after R0, with no boot-settle gate. Spike 3 measured about 1 GiB of boot-settle pool growth on this PC, and its own harness waited for a settle (V2, settle_6) for that reason. Fed 1 GiB of settle spread over the first 12 of I0's 20 gaps, -Report gives OUTCOME VOID (I0 905,785 B/s against I1 11,000 B/s). Spread over 9 or fewer gaps, the burst filter absorbs it and the run reads A. So the single-use Restart session goes VOID whenever the settle outlasts about half of I0.
2. **(minor)** -Prepare's check that the no-link walker skips C:\Users\All Users runs robocopy with /LEV:2. At that depth 'All Users\Microsoft' can never appear, so the check passes whether or not /XJ is given. With /LEV:3 the check tells the two apart. /XJ does skip a directory symlink (I measured that), so nothing leaks today; the check just cannot catch it if it ever did.
3. **(minor)** The FILTERS line reads 'recorded' for an fltmc.txt holding unelevated fltmc's 'Filter listing failed with error: 0x80070005 / Access is denied.'

All scratch folders I created were removed.

findings.evidence: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:531-533 (required marks list no F*/X*), :537 (only a null exitCode VOIDs), :591-603, :620, :650-663; reproduced with hand-built marks.jsonl/arms.jsonl run through `pwsh -File tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 -Report -NoWrite -RunDir <dir>`: baseline A/PASS, 'F3 exit 70, no report' A/PASS, 'no exe arms at all' A/PASS
findings.fix:
In Get-Verdict, before the exe judgement, add four checks:
- Return UNDECIDED unless there are exactly five exe-full arms and five exe-cancel/exe-close arms, each with before and settled marks.
- Return UNDECIDED (or FAIL) naming the arm when an exe-full arm has exitCode != 0, a null report, or report.status != 'Completed'.
- Count `guardStop` on any S/P/exe arm as over T, the way L's already is.
- Add 'full-run-crashed', 'exe-runs-missing' and 'exe-guard-stop' rows to PoolWatchReportTests.TheReportRoutesARunAsTheToleranceRowSays.

findings.claim:
PoolWatch -Protocol takes R0 and goes straight into the 20-minute I0 idle window (PoolWatch.ps1:836-837). -Protocol must start within 30 min of boot (:829), so I0 falls in the boot settle. Spike 3 measured the settle on this PC: 'About 1 GiB of that growth came during the boot settle, before L started', with R_start 1.3 min after boot. Its harness waited for a settle first ('V2 passes: the settle was reached at settle_6').

-Report VOIDs a run when I0's and I1's drift differ by more than 3x (:547-550). The burst filter (:498) only drops gaps over 3x the median, so it removes a settle confined to a minority of gaps but not one spread over most of I0.

Measured on hand-built run logs, with idle drift otherwise 11,000 B/s as spike 3 recorded:
- 1 GiB spread over the first 6 or 9 of I0's 20 gaps reads A/PASS.
- Spread over the first 12 it reads 'OUTCOME VOID — idle drift of pagedBytes disagrees between I0 (9,05,785 B/s) and I1 (11,000 B/s)'.

The outcome of the person's single Restart-and-4-hour session therefore depends on how long their boot takes to settle, which nothing in the protocol controls.
findings.evidence: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:829 (boot age at most 1800 s), :836-837 (`$script:R0 = Write-Mark 'R0'; Wait-Idle 'I0' ...`, nothing between them), :498 (burst rule), :547-550 (VOID on drift disagreement); spike fresh-boot-cold-c-listing-vs-sizeprobe-vs-plain-open evidence (R_start 1.3 min after boot, ~1 GiB settle growth, V2 settle_6); -Report run on generated marks with a 1 GiB I0 ramp over 0/6/9/12 gaps gave A, A, A, VOID
findings.fix: Between R0 and I0 in -Protocol, add a settle phase. Take a `settle/NN` mark every MarkEverySec until two consecutive gaps move each pool by less than 16 MiB (spike 3's V2 rule), with a cap of about 30 min. Start I0 only after that. R0 stays the boot-age and guard reference. Record the settle marks in the run log and in the tolerance row's text.

findings.claim:
-Prepare's X3 check that 'the no-link walker does not descend C:\Users\All Users' cannot fail.

It runs `robocopy C:\Users ... /L /E /XJ ... /LEV:2` and passes when the log lacks 'All Users\Microsoft'. With /LEV:2, robocopy processes only C:\Users and its direct children, so a level-3 path like All Users\Microsoft is never logged, with or without /XJ. The result `noLinkWalkerSkipsAllUsers` is therefore always true. It also runs its own command line rather than Invoke-NoLinkWalk, so it says nothing about the walker the protocol actually uses.

Measured on a %TEMP% tree with an 'All Users' junction to a folder holding Microsoft\deep:
- /LEV:2 without /XJ logs no 'All Users\Microsoft' and the check would say 'skips'.
- /LEV:3 without /XJ does log it.
- /XJ skips both a junction and a directory symlink (C:\Users\All Users is a SymbolicLink).

So the walker is safe today, but the safeguard X3 asked for cannot detect a regression.
findings.evidence: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:792-793; robocopy runs on %TEMP%\cr-sl095-lev (since removed): 'LEV2 no XJ ... = True' (vacuous), 'LEV3 no XJ: walks ... = True', 'LEV3 /XJ ... = False', 'no LEV /XJ: walks Sym Users\Microsoft = False'
findings.fix: Run the check through Invoke-NoLinkWalk itself, or at least with /LEV:3 so a followed link would show. Have -Protocol refuse to start when prepare.json records noLinkWalkerSkipsAllUsers false.

findings.claim: Get-FiltersLine (and the fltmcFilters field Get-EnvironmentRecord copies from the same file) treats any non-blank fltmc.txt as the pasted filter list. Unelevated `fltmc filters` prints 'Filter listing failed with error: 0x80070005 / Access is denied.' If a person pastes that, which is what this machine prints without elevation, -Report says 'FILTERS recorded: ...fltmc.txt'. Criterion 3's filter list is then marked recorded when no filter was listed, against the build's own rule that a missing paste reads UNDECIDED, never recorded.
findings.evidence: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:670-682 (Get-FiltersLine: `@(Get-Content $f | Where-Object { $_.Trim() }).Count`), :340 (fltmcFilters = @(Get-Content fltmc.txt)); measured: `fltmc filters 2>&1 > fltmc.txt` then `PoolWatch.ps1 -Report -NoWrite` printed 'FILTERS recorded: C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\cr-sl095-fltmc\fltmc.txt'
findings.fix: Count the paste as recorded only when it contains fltmc's header line (`^\s*Filter Name\s+Num Instances`). Otherwise, or when it matches `0x8007|Access is denied|failed`, print 'FILTERS UNDECIDED: fltmc.txt holds no filter list (<first line>)'. Add that case to MissingOrNullReadingsAreUndecidedAndABurstGapIsLeftOutOfDrift.

obligations.evidence: Ran `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-095-ContainerLayerWalk/SL-095-ContainerLayerWalk.Tests.csproj`: 1 passed, 0 skipped, exit 0, against the real C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers.

The precondition is false, not unproven. docs/design/SL-095-container-layer-store.md:159 records that the dynamic base image holds real pristine copies, so real bytes go uncounted. The code accommodates this instead of proving it: TopLevelRowText.cs and UnreadableRows.NotScannedText say 'size not counted', Q-180/Q-181 accept the shortfall, and -Prepare takes a robocopy /XJ upper bound once. Validate should record it as disproved and accepted, not discharged.

The in-scan paths are closed in code:
- DirectoryReader.Read refuses and counts anything at or under the store (DirectoryReader.cs:94-98).
- The fitness rule 'every directory open goes through the guarded call in DirectoryReader' holds.
- Links are never followed.

Loopback SMB (\\localhost\C$) and other WCI stores are explicitly not covered (ContainerLayerStore.cs remarks). Only the post-Restart protocol's WCIFS-UNATTRIBUTED clause can measure the rest, and it has not run.

The repro, X-002 and X-004 list Containers, ContainerStorages and BaseImages, but only on this already-touched boot, where first-touch leaks read 0. Only the post-Restart protocol (L's WCsc against the idle envelope, then the closing control) can show it. Not run.

It asserts the record and an empty Unreadable list. Its docstring's 'its row says so' is not asserted at TopLevel level, but the App's row is built from SkippedStores.
ARootAtOrInsideTheStoreIsRefused has rows for the store, \L1 and the deep Speech folder: Refused, ScanRefusal.ContainerLayerStore, 0 calls on the scan's guard, an empty store.

ARootInsideTheStoreInAnotherSpellingIsRefusedWithNoOpen calls Resolve with an already-cancelled token, so any open would abort and give None. A Refuse therefore proves the zero-open string step decided the \\?\, trailing, lower and upper spellings.

WithNoStoreTheScanIsWhatItWasBefore points the override at an absent x\Containers\Layers and compares with a precaution-off scan: same totals, entry count and unreadable count. Resolve never checks existence (it gives Exclude), but the scan is identical, which is what the case's why requires.

ARootTheResolutionCannotOpenIsTheUsualRootUnreadable: a missing root (Resolve gives None, asserted directly) and an ACL-denied root both end RootUnreadable with no exception. The UNC and 'GetFinalPathNameByHandleW fails after a good open' sub-shapes are not fed (no seam). They share the same null return in FinalPath.

tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-X001 runs the published exe through read-window.ps1 on the real $env:ProgramData store path in 3 spellings. It asserts outcome=refused, refusal=container-layer-store, EXIT 0, 0 files and folders, and the precaution on. The engine ran it (O-061); I did not.

tests/bugs/SL-095-ContainerLayerWalk roots at the real C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers, with the live layer 1f35079a present, and fails on any listing inside Layers\<id>\Files. I ran it: 1 passed, exit 0.

PoolWatchReportTests control-leaks-zero builds a closing control arm with WCsc rise 0 over 50 entries. Both the Theory and ARunOnABootThatAlreadyWalkedTheLayerIsVoidNeverPass assert 'OUTCOME VOID' with the not-armable reason and no PASS.

Marked non-material and deliberately untested. The reason still holds: on the handle step, OpenForFinalPath (SynchronousIoCancel.cs) is a single FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES | BACKUP_SEMANTICS open of the root. The anchor is %ProgramData%, never the store. The refusal follows before any listing.

drift: ContainerLayerStore.Resolve never checks that the store exists. The design contract says 'The store is absent: None', but on a PC without one Resolve returns Exclude for a root above the path, or Refuse for a root at it. The walk simply never meets the path, so behaviour is unchanged (WithNoStoreTheScanIsWhatItWasBefore). Not declared.

A refused root is not refused before the App starts a scan. The App enters the scanning state (ScanningPanel 'Reading <path>', Cancel enabled, timer running) until Core returns Refused. It then shows the refusal through ShowProblem in the could-not-read colours, with the full Defect paragraph. The design said 'enters no scanning state and opens no dialog' and a status line. This follows from deciding the refusal in Core. Not declared.

The closing layer control is still `cmd /c dir /a /s /b` (PoolWatch.ps1:877), while X3's decision text says every dir control goes through a walker that does not follow links. The build keeps the subtrees link-free instead: -Prepare rejects any subtree with a reparse-point directory, which is X3's second half. Every other non-app walk is robocopy /XJ.

Attempt 3 itself departs from nothing new beyond its four declared deviations. Attempt 2's eight departures (NotScanned flag instead of an EntryKind, pop-time check, Precautions switch, count-only report fields, 8.3 via GetFullPath, no report on a closed window, FSA_HOOK_HOLD_S not built, smoke trigger roots) are all declared in build-slice-2.json.

Nothing new departed from the design in this round. The missing settle gate (N1) follows the design's own protocol order ('R0, then I0: 20 min idle'), so the gap is inherited from the design rather than introduced by the build. The design dropped the settle phase that spike 3's harness ran (V2).
